features.title: Hand the frame's regions to plugin surfaces
features.summary: The owned stack always gives shell.main to Workbench tabs, without a user-selectable native layout. The frame supplies its authorized keyed-main renderer, recursion guard and an absent-occupant native fallback. shell.dock owns a fullheight right pane across both grid rows; collapsing it hides persistent mounted tabs and a separate native resource carrier, never reveals native chrome. Registered DockPaneActions serve the main Pane options Open right pane item (closed only), pane-local Close pane icons and original keyboard control; the centre never offers Close right pane. Workbench owns quiet group chrome and real split groups; the frame adds no toolbar. ctx.frameBottom opens only the left/centre bottom row, preserving right-pane geometry.
failureModes: A frame that offers no seat leaves ctx.rightPanel absent, so a dock plugin stays inert instead of failing.
Closing the Workbench right pane must hide its mounted shell.dock tabs and native resource carrier, not expose a second native surface or accept stale native geometry reports.
An empty shell.main seat falls back to the selected native main panel.
The delegated keyed renderer returns null for dshfiles-workbench rather than recursively mounting the workbench inside itself.
A stock frame leaves ctx.mainSurface absent; consumers must check the optional face.

externalDependencies.boundary: The genuine native sidebar remains a hidden Session/resource carrier under Workbench. It reports presentation through ctx.layout only in absent-Workbench compatibility deployments; Workbench alone reports visible right-pane geometry.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: The seat's store, internal compatibility tokens and action registration are exercised directly in src/right-panel.test.ts; scratch journeys exercise the real Workbench right pane.

features.title: Persist the frame's dragged panel widths
features.summary: The layout bundle keeps dragged sidebar and right-panel widths in the browser, so a reload restores the sidebar's last open width and the right panel's px preference. Workbench separately owns visibility of its persistent fullheight right-pane tabs; frame geometry does not select native chrome.

features.title: Persist the collapsed sidebar
features.summary: Closing the left sidebar is remembered: a reload boots it collapsed, and reopening restores the last open width instead of the 280px contract default. The owned frameSidebar.show presentation port reveals it idempotently from live frame state, so repeated Reset layout calls cannot toggle it closed again.

features.title: Give the stage the full width on a phone
features.summary: When the left-column occupant marks the document with data-shell-phone-nav, a frame narrower than 640px drops the sidebar and right tracks, hides the sidebar drag handle and shortens itself by --dsh-phone-nav-height so the occupant's bottom tab bar never covers the composer. Without the mark the frame keeps upstream behaviour.

failureModes: An occupant that sets the mark without drawing navigation would hide the thread list; only the thread sidebar's fixed layout sets it.

features.title: One status strip at the bottom of the frame
features.summary: A thin row under every column where plugins add at most one text-first item each through the @dshfiles/frame-layout/status-strip registry: global items on the left, items about the open thread on the right. It stays empty (zero height) until an item is added, an item that throws hides only itself, and on a phone-width frame it collapses to one Status chip that opens the items as a list; with the phone shell present (plans/ade-ux §8 phase 6) that chip is a 44px dot in the top bar's trailing corner and the list drops below the bar, so no strip row sits between the stage and the tab bar.
failureModes: A second item from the same plugin id is ignored, so one plugin cannot fill the strip.
A provider whose component throws is hidden by its own boundary and logged; the frame keeps rendering.

features.title: Show, hide and reorder status bar items
features.summary: Settings › General › Status bar lists every registered status item with a show switch and up/down buttons; right-clicking an item in the strip offers Hide this item and Status bar settings…. The choice is stored in the dshfiles-frame-layout settings namespace as hiddenStatusItems and statusItemOrder (so settings_set covers agent writes); ids nobody registers are ignored and a newly added item appears at its default place.

features.title: Click a status item to open its page
features.summary: A status item may declare open: the strip renders it as a button that opens its full page (Working: the thread list on its Working view; Restart: the Plugins page with the HMR updates row) and its context menu offers Open <label>. An item that draws its own buttons (Quota) declares controls, so its meters keep their popover and Open Quota (Usage › Quota) stays in the context menu.
failureModes: An item whose component renders nothing leaves no empty button behind: the wrapper hides with it.
